subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class bounded memory CRUD write contract to memory-core, and what limit, identity, duplicate/consolidation, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: The capability gap is clear in source, but adding it defines a new persistent memory write API plus security and upgrade behavior that automation should not choose.

options.title: Define memory-core bounded CRUD
options.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, hard limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, and secret policy before code lands.

options.title: Limit scope to existing paths
options.body: Keep first-class CRUD out of core for now and address bloat through memory-flush, dreaming promotion, bootstrap, and recall limits only.

options.title: Prototype outside core first
options.body: Ask contributors to prove the write policy as a memory plugin or ClawHub package until a missing core/plugin API is concrete.

recommendation.title: Define memory-core bounded CRUD
recommendation.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, hard limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, and secret policy before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core tool, state, and validation history makes this the best available routing candidate for the product/API decision.
